Our Company’s inventories primarily consist of soyabeans (raw material), soya meal, and edible oils (finished goods). The days of inventory holding have been computed based on our historical Restated Standalone Financial Information, which reflects seasonal demand patterns and operational requirements. For Fiscal 2027, 2028, and 2029, our Company has assumed inventory holding levels of 103 days, 96 days, and 97 days of cost of material consumed, respectively. These assumptions are consistent with historical inventory trends as well as considering the proposed expansion plans and our experience in managing inventory during peak and non-peak seasons. In Fiscal 2026, inventory holding reached up to 83 days, with a mean of 77 days over the last three fiscals. Accordingly, inventory levels for Fiscals 2027, 2028, and 2029 have been projected in line with past trends as well as considering the proposed expansion plans, , thereby ensuring alignment with anticipated production schedules and the expected customer demand. The projected holding levels factor in the additional soyabean inventory required to be carried against our forward export contracts for food-grade soya products, which have delivery schedules of four to 6 six months and require raw material to be procured and hedged upfront, as well as the higher finished goods inventory to be maintained across multiple SKUs of consumer packs. This further reflect the separate inventories required to be maintained for our food grade and feed grade soya meal products across varying protein contents, which are not interchangeable and accordingly entail longer holding periods.

Soyabean seeds stored in the silos are discharged through belt conveyors and bucket elevators into the preparatory section at a controlled feed rate.
Seeds pass through vibrating screens, destoners and separators to remove sticks, dust, foreign material and stones, protecting downstream equipment and improving product purity.
Cleaned soyabean seeds (By-products: sticks, foreign material and stones)
Cleaned seeds are cracked between roller mills into pieces,
loosening the hull and exposing the oil-bearing cells.
Cracked material is aspirated over hull separators; the lighter hulls are drawn off, raising the protein content of the resultant meal.
Dehulled meats; (Soyabean hulls recovered as a saleable output)
Meats are heated with steam in a stack cooker to approximately 60–70 °C at controlled moisture, rupturing the oil cells, coagulating the proteins and rendering the material for flaking.

Conditioned meats are passed through smooth flaking rolls and rolled into thin flakes of about 0.25–0.35 mm, shortening the path the solvent must travel to reach the oil thus improving oil Extraction.
Flakes are extruded through an expander with steam injection to form porous collets of higher bulk density, improving solvent percolation and extraction efficiency and reducing solvent retention.

Collets are conveyed to the extractor and washed counter-currently with food-grade hexane, which dissolves the oil to form miscella; the extracted solids leave the extractor as solvent-wet de-oiled cake.
Miscella (oil + hexane) and solvent-wet de-oiled cake
Miscella is heated through the economiser, distillation columns and stripper under vacuum to evaporate the hexane from the oil; the hexane vapours are condensed and returned to the process for reuse.
Soya crude oil; (recovered hexane recycled to extraction)
Solvent-wet de-oiled cake is treated with direct and indirect steam in the desolventiser–toaster to strip residual hexane and toast the meal,
Desolventised and toasted soya meal (by-product: residual hexane vapours recovered)
deactivating anti- nutritional factors. Hexane vapours are condensed and the hexane recovered.
Toasted meal is dried to the targeted moisture in the dryer section and then cooled with ambient air to near-ambient temperature, preventing caking and microbial growth during storage.
Dried and cooled soya meal (by-product: moisture vented)
Cooled meal is passed through grading screens and a hammer mill to achieve uniform particle size and to remove oversized lumps before dispatch.
Graded meal is weighed on calibrated bagging scales, filled into various packages such as PP bags, bulk in FIBC bags for dispatch.
Packed soyabean meal ready for dispatch
Feed the refinery with crude oil
Soya crude oil received from the solvent extraction plant is filtered, weighed and held in the crude oil storage tank, from where it is pumped to the refinery at a controlled flow rate.

Crude oil is heated and dosed with a measured quantity of hot water (and phosphoric acid where required) under agitation for a fixed retention period, hydrating the phospholipids so that they become insoluble in oil.
The hydrated mass is passed through a centrifugal separator, which separates the heavier gum phase from the degummed oil. The gums recovered are further processed into lecithin.
Degummed oil; gums recovered and processed to lecithin

Degummed oil is dosed with caustic soda (lye) in a mixer and retained in the neutraliser; the caustic reacts with the free fatty acids to form soap stock, which is separated in a centrifugal separator and washed.
Neutralised oil; soap stock, further split into acid oil
Washed neutralised oil is dried under vacuum at elevated temperature to strip residual moisture, preventing hydrolysis and ensuring efficient bleaching downstream.
Removal of colour pigments and trace impurities

Dried oil is contacted with activated bleaching earth (and activated carbon where required) in the bleacher under vacuum and controlled temperature, adsorbing colour pigments, residual soap, and oxidation products.
Bleached oil with spent earth in suspension
Bleached oil is filtered through pressure leaf filters to retain the spent bleaching earth; the cake is blown down and discharged, and the recovered oil is returned to the process.
Filtered bleached oil (by-product: spent earth cake)
Filtered oil is passed through a polish filter to remove fine residual earth particles, ensuring a clear feed to the deodoriser.
Removal of dissolved air and moisture
Oil is deaerated under vacuum before heating, removing dissolved oxygen and moisture, which prevents oxidation at deodorisation temperature.
Removal of odour and volatile compounds
Deaerated oil is heated under high vacuum and stripped with
sparge steam in the deodoriser to remove free fatty acids, odoriferous and volatile compounds, and is then cooled through heat recovery.
Cooled deodorised oil is passed through the final polish filter to remove any residual particulate matter before storage, ensuring clarity and brightness of the finished oil.
Polished refined oil is transferred to the refined oil storage tanks and retained pending quality clearance.

Quality-cleared refined oil is conveyed to the packing unit and filled into pouches, bottles, jars and tins in different SKUs on calibrated filling lines, then coded, cartoned and stacked for dispatch.
Packed refined soya oil ready for distribution

Accepted meal is conveyed by elevators to the raw material silo, where it is held under controlled conditions and drawn down at a steady rate
Stored soya meal ready for grinding
so that the grinding line receives a uniform, homogeneous feed.

Meal is fed through a magnetic separator and metered into the grinder/pulveriser, where it is reduced to a fine powder at controlled temperature and feed rate to protect protein quality; the aspiration system controls dust and heat build- up.
Ground flour is pneumatically conveyed to the finished goods silo, where it is held to equalise temperature and moisture and to provide surge capacity between grinding and grading.
Stabilised ground soya flour in storage
Particle size classification and quality control

Flour is drawn from the finished goods silo and passed over vibratory sifters/gyro screens fitted with the specified mesh to classify it to the required particle size; oversize material is returned to grinding, and in-line magnets remove any tramp iron.
Graded defatted soya flour to specification (oversize recycled to grinding)
Graded flour meeting the specified protein content, particle size, moisture and microbiological parameters is released by quality control as finished product.

Released flour is weighed on calibrated bagging scales and filled into bags or containers of the specified SKU, stitched or sealed, coded with batch and date details, and stacked in the finished-goods godown for dispatch to food and industrial customers.
Packed defatted soya flour ready for dispatch

Untoasted (white flake) soya meal drawn from the solvent extraction plant is weighed, sampled and tested for protein content, PDI/NSI, moisture and freedom from foreign matter before acceptance, the untoasted grade being essential to retain the protein functionality required for texturisation.
Accepted meal is conveyed to the raw material silo and held under controlled conditions, being drawn down at a steady rate so that the milling line receives a homogeneous feed.

Meal is passed through a magnetic separator and metered into the air classifier mill, where impact milling combined with air classification produces a fine, uniform particle size at controlled temperature; coarse fractions are internally recirculated for regrinding.
Milled and classified soya meal of uniform particle size
Milled meal is dosed with metered water and direct
steam in the pre-conditioner under agitation, hydrating and pre-heating the protein to the required moisture and temperature so that it plasticises uniformly in the extruder.

Pre-conditioned meal is fed to the twin-screw extruder, where controlled shear, temperature and pressure denature and realign the protein; on discharge through the die the sudden pressure drop expands the mass, and the rotating cutter sizes it into chunks, granules or flakes as required.
Extrudate is passed over vibratory sifters to classify it into the required size fractions and to separate fines and oversize; oversize is returned for re-sizing and fines are recovered.
Removal of fines and surface dust

Graded material is passed through the polish/aspiration stage, where an air stream lifts adhering fines and surface dust from the granules, giving a clean, free-flowing product and improved appearance.
Polished textured protein granules (by- product: fines recovered)

Polished product is dried in the dryer to the target moisture and then cooled with filtered ambient air to near-ambient temperature, arresting further cooking and preventing condensation, caking and microbial growth in storage.
Dried and cooled textured soya protein
Dried and cooled product meeting the specified protein content, texture, water absorption, particle size, moisture and microbiological parameters is released by quality control as finished product.

Refined Sunflower Oil is a premium, light, and nutritious cooking oil extracted from sunflower seeds and refined for purity and safety. It features a mild, neutral flavor and a high smoke point, making it ideal for frying, sautéing, baking, and industrial food applications. Rich in Vitamin E and essential fatty acids, it supports heart health and acts as a natural antioxidant, enhancing the shelf life and quality of food products. Its low saturated fat content and absence of trans fats and cholesterol make it a heart-friendly choice for health-conscious consumers. Widely used in snacks, ready-to-eat foods, confectionery, and processed food manufacturing. Offered in a range of packaging formats tailored for both industrial and retail use, refined sunflower oil is a cost-effective and reliable solution for diverse culinary and commercial needs.

Soya Crude Oil is a high-quality, unrefined vegetable oil extracted from soya beans using solvent extraction methods. It is widely used as a primary raw material for refining into edible oil. Additionally, crude soya oil is a valuable ingredient in animal feed formulations due to its high energy content and nutritional profile, particularly its richness in essential fatty acids and natural tocopherols (Vitamin E). With a balanced fatty acid composition and natural antioxidant properties, it contributes to the overall health and growth performance of livestock and poultry.

Soya Crude Oil is the key raw material for producing Refined Edible Soya bean Oil through a multi-step refining process, making it suitable for cooking and food processing. Rich in polyunsaturated fats and free from trans fats and cholesterol, refined soya bean oil is a heart-healthy choice. Crude Soya Oil to some extent is also used in animal feed due to its high energy content and essential fatty acids. It enhances feed palatability, promotes growth, and supports immunity in livestock. Its natural Vitamin E content aids in metabolism and nutrient absorption, making it a cost-effective input for both food and feed industries.

Soya bean Protein based products for Food Applications: We also offer high quality food grade soya meal i.e. non-GMO defatted toasted and untoasted soya flakes and grits suitable for use in as a protein fortifying ingredient in many food manufacturing processes. Food grade soya meal is produced by crushing high quality soya beans to remove oil through solvent extraction, followed by refining, drying and milling to ensure high protein content and safety for human consumption. Soya flakes and soya grits are used by food manufacturers such as soya sauce, soya nuggets, soya flour, TSP etc. We market these products under our owned brand “MOEL”. As a part of forward-integrated strategy, we are also manufacturing and selling soya bean value-added products such as soya flour and TSP

in FY26, despite some volatility during FY20–FY22, reflecting fluctuations in soybean availability, processing volumes and soybean meal prices. Toasted Soya Flakes are premium-quality, defatted flakes made from carefully selected non-GMO soyabeans. Subjected to a precise toasting process, these flakes develop a rich, nutty flavor and enhanced digestibility, making them an excellent source of plant- based protein. They are widely used in the production of fermented soya sauce in Southeast Asian countries and serve as a versatile ingredient in granola, cereals, protein bars, meat analogs, and bakery products. With their crunchy texture, high protein content, and excellent water absorption and binding properties, Toasted Soya Flakes improve both the nutritional profile and mouthfeel of a variety of food applications. Ideal for health-conscious consumers and food manufacturers seeking clean-label, protein-rich ingredients, they are available in bulk packaging with a long shelf life, ensuring convenience and reliability in large-scale production. Untoasted Soya Flakes are defatted soya flakes made from non-GMO soya beans, processed without heat treatment to retain their natural color, neutral taste, and native functional properties. With a mild flavor profile and high protein concentration, they are ideal for applications that require custom processing, such as protein concentrates, fermentation bases, or rehydrated formulations. These flakes are commonly used in nutritional supplements, functional food blends, meat substitutes, and other plant- based food applications where flavor control and ingredient adaptability are essential. Their excellent binding and moisture-holding capacity contributes to improved texture and consistency in diverse product matrices. Preferred by food manufacturers looking for cost-effective, clean-label, high-protein solutions, Untoasted Soya Flakes offer processing flexibility and are supplied in bulk quantities with extended shelf life. Toasted Soya Grits are high-protein soya fragments produced from non-GMO soya beans through a gentle toasting process that enhances their flavor, aroma, digestibility,

and nutritional value. With a distinct nutty taste and crunchy texture, they are widely used in snack foods, cereals, bakery products, and plant-based formulations. The toasting process improves shelf life and functionality, making them ideal for protein fortification and texture enhancement. They are also used in soya sauce fermentation, meat analogues, nutritional blends, and health-focused diets, catering to both food manufacturers and health-conscious consumers seeking a clean- label, nutrient-dense ingredient. Untoasted Soya Grits are coarse, protein- rich fragments derived from non-GMO soya beans, minimally processed to retain their natural nutrition. They offer a neutral flavor and are commonly used in baking, meat substitutes, nutritional supplements, and industrial soya protein applications where toasting is not desired or toasting is done further in the Food Industry. Due to their high protein content, they are ideal for protein enrichment, especially in formulations requiring further processing or heat treatment. Their versatility and functional properties make them a staple ingredient in health foods, ready mixes, and fortified formulations, supporting clean-label and plant-based product development. Toasted Soya Flour are made from high- quality, non-genetically modified soya beans after oil extraction and is processed through controlled toasting. The toasting process enhances the flavor, reduces anti-nutritional factors, and improves digestibility. It offers a rich, nutty aroma and is a valuable source of protein, fiber, and essential nutrients. Ideal for use in baked goods, extruded snacks, protein bars, and nutritional supplements, it improves texture, flavor, and shelf life. Its functional properties, including emulsification and moisture retention, make it a versatile ingredient for both industrial and household food applications. Untoasted Soya Flour are high-quality, nutrient-rich powder derived from non- genetically modified soya beans after oil extraction. It retains high protein content and natural enzyme activity, making it suitable for fermentation and functional food applications. Ideal for making textured products, it enhances flavour and nutritional value in baking, gluten-free recipes, breads, smoothies, and savoury dishes. Its excellent
water absorption and binding properties improve texture and consistency in various formulations. This versatile flour supports clean-label, high-protein, and allergen- friendly food innovations.

Textured Soya Protein (“TSP”) is also known as Textured Vegetable Protein (“TVP”), is a plant-based protein derived from Non-GMO, defatted soya flour or soya protein concentrate through an extrusion process. Known for its high protein content (up to 50–70%) and multi-functional uses, TSP serves as an excellent meat substitute and dietary protein source. It is widely used in a variety of applications including high- protein dietary foods, meat alternatives, breakfast cereals, confectionery, breakfast bowls, and processed food products. Its meat- like texture, excellent water absorption, and flavor retention capabilities make it ideal for both savory and sweet formulations. TSP is cholesterol-free, low in fat, and supports clean-label, high-protein product development.

Animal feed ingredients: We offer feed grade soya bean meal (deoiled cake), low fat meal, full fat meal and soya hulls. Soya bean meal is the residue of the soya bean seed after the oil has been extracted. In addition to regular soya bean meal, we also produce a specialised high-protein feed grade soya bean meal (hi-pro) depending on the customer’s requirement which contains higher protein than regular soya bean meal, and subsequently higher metabolisable energy. The products produced under this category are marketed under brand name “MOEL” and majorly catered to the poultry, dairy, livestock and aquaculture feed industry. With low oil and low fiber content, it ensures better and enhanced feed efficiency. Rich in vital nutrients, it supports muscle growth, immunity, and overall animal health. Non-GMO soya defatted soya meal is a nutrient-rich byproduct obtained after the extraction of oil from non-genetically modified soya beans. High in protein and fiber, they serve as an excellent ingredient for animal feed, poultry feed, and aquaculture diets. With enhanced digestibility and rich in amino acids, they promote healthy growth in livestock. These meal act as a cost-effective protein supplement in feed formulations. Free from artificial additives and GMOs, they support natural and sustainable farming practices. Ideal for cattle, poultry, and fish nutrition, ensuring optimal health and productivity. Available in bulk packaging with a long shelf life. Perfect for use in the feed industry as a high-protein, sustainable alternative.

Soya hulls/husks are the outer shells of soya beans, obtained during soya bean processing. They are rich in fiber and serve as an excellent source of roughage for animal feed. With high digestibility and nutrient content, they improve gut health in livestock. Commonly used in cattle, poultry, and swine feed, they enhance feed efficiency. Low in protein but high in energy, they act as a cost- effective alternative to traditional fiber sources. Free from artificial additives, they support natural and sustainable farming. Available in bulk packaging, they should be stored in a dry place. Ideal for animal nutrition and feed industry applications.

Full Fat Soya Oil Cake is a protein-rich by- product obtained after mechanical pressing (expelling) of whole soya beans, without solvent extraction. It retains both protein and natural oil content, making it a high-energy, high-protein feed ingredient. Typically used in animal and poultry feed, it contains 38– 42% protein and 16–19% oil, along with essential amino acids and fiber. Being Non- GMO and naturally processed, it supports healthy growth, improved digestion, and enhanced feed efficiency. Its balanced nutritional profile makes it a preferred choice in livestock, poultry, and aquaculture nutrition formulations.

These characteristics make it an essential ingredient in the food industry, particularly in products like chocolates, confectionery, and bakery items. Soya bean Lecithin is a natural emulsifier which is produced during refining of soya oil process. It has many functional properties like emulsification and food binding which makes it a crucial functional ingredient in food

industry like chocolate, confectionery and bakery. It may be used in pharma and cosmetics. Additionally, lecithin finds applications in animal feed for better nutrient absorption and in industrial processes as a lubricant and release agent. Its versatility, cost-effectiveness, and natural origin make it an indispensable ingredient across multiple sectors. Available in liquid and powder forms for diverse applications.
